page: Microsoft Azure M416-208s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processors operating at 2.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 104 physical cores, 208 vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, and a massive 5700.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 27.4 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with an 8389 GB SSD, and the instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution are highly performant, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, reaching top-tier status for both cached small-block reads at 10446.46 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 651.24 GB/sec and writes at 347.19 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a high-density resource profile where the cost is heavily weighted toward its massive memory capacity and local SSD storage rather than raw single-threaded compute speed. The tradeoff involves accepting lower single-core efficiency in exchange for massive memory capacity and high-throughput parallel processing. This profile is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments achieving top-tier SET operations at 162.62 million operations per second, heavy database operations, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads.
